question: Xanthia can read 100 pages per hour and Molly can read 50 pages per hour. If they each read the same book, and the book has 225 pages, how many more minutes than Xanthia would it take for Molly to finish reading the book?

Xanthia reads at a rate of 100 pages per hour. Therefore, her time to read 225 pages is:
\[
\text{Time for Xanthia} = \frac{225 \text{ pages}}{100 \text{ pages/hour}} = 2.25 \text{ hours}
\]
Converting 2.25 hours to minutes:
\[
2.25 \text{ hours} \times 60 \text{ minutes/hour} = 135 \text{ minutes}
\]

Molly reads at a rate of 50 pages per hour. Therefore, her time to read 225 pages is:
\[
\text{Time for Molly} = \frac{225 \text{ pages}}{50 \text{ pages/hour}} = 4.5 \text{ hours}
\]
Converting 4.5 hours to minutes:
\[
4.5 \text{ hours} \times 60 \text{ minutes/hour} = 270 \text{ minutes}
\]

The difference in time between Molly and Xanthia is:
\[
270 \text{ minutes} - 135 \text{ minutes} = 135 \text{ minutes}
\]

Thus, it takes Molly \(\boxed{135}\) more minutes than Xanthia to finish reading the book.
